name: Universal Dependencies relations
source: The 37 universal syntactic relations of Universal Dependencies v2 (universaldependencies.org/u/dep). Typed in from Claude's memory of that table, not copied from the site: the names and groups are likely right, the plain-language meanings and the Mandarin examples are Claude's own and not checked.
use: Phase 7: each grammar pattern links to the relations it builds, so the dictionary can say which kinds of dependency Hao-shuo-de has and which it leaves out.

items.meaning: the one who does or is (the subject of a clause)
the thing acted on (the object)
the one who gets the thing (the second object)
a whole clause that is the subject
a clause that is the object, with its own subject
a clause that is the object and shares the subject of the main verb
a noun that says where, when, with what or for whom (not an argument)
the person spoken to, named in the sentence
an empty subject word that stands for nothing (English 'it' in 'it rains')
a topic put at the front and picked up later in the clause

example.en: This book, I have read it.
example.head: 看

items.meaning: a clause that works like an adverb (because, if, when)
a word that says how, how much or when
a word that carries tone, not content (particles like 吧, 啊)
a helper verb (can, will, must)
the linking verb 'be' between a thing and what it is
a word that opens a clause (if, that, because)
a noun that tells more about another noun (whose, of what)
a second name or description for the same thing
a number that counts a noun
a clause that tells more about a noun (a relative clause)
a describing word for a noun
a word that says which one (this, that, every)
a counting word between a number and a noun (本, 个)
a word that marks the role of a noun (in, at, of): a preposition, postposition or 的
the second thing in a list joined by and / or
the joining word (and, or, but)
a fixed phrase that works as one function word
items.note: Claude does not remember a safe Mandarin example.

items.meaning: a name or date written in parts with no head inside
a compound word built from two words
items in a list that are not joined by a word
two clauses side by side, with no word that says how they relate
what is left after a repeated verb is dropped (gapping)
the pieces of one word that was spelled in two
items.note: A spelling problem, not found in Mandarin.

items.meaning: a word that the speaker took back
punctuation
the head of the whole sentence
a link whose kind could not be settled
items.note: A fallback, not a kind of grammar.
